qe: Following the sudden suspension of the Non-Cooperation Movement, a distinct group of Congress leaders advocated ending the boycott of legislative councils to enter them and obstruct the government. Who spearheaded this school of thought?
qh: असहयोग आंदोलन के अचानक स्थगन के बाद, कांग्रेस नेताओं के एक विशिष्ट समूह ने विधायी परिषदों का बहिष्कार समाप्त करने, उनमें प्रवेश करने और सरकार को बाधित करने की वकालत की। इस विचारधारा का नेतृत्व किसने किया था?
o: C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru, and Ajmal Khan
C. Rajagopalachari, Vallabhbhai Patel, and Rajendra Prasad
Lala Lajpat Rai, Madan Mohan Malaviya, and N.C. Kelkar
Ananda Mohan Bose, Shibchandra Deb, and Umesh Chandra Datta
e: Detailed Explanation: Following Gandhi's arrest in March 1922, the nationalist ranks faced a political vacuum. C.R. Das, Motilal Nehru, and Ajmal Khan advocated entry into the legislative councils to use them as an arena of political struggle, earning the label 'Swarajists'.

qe: The Congress leaders who strongly opposed the proposal of council entry, choosing instead to focus entirely on constructive work and non-cooperation, were historically labeled as:
qh: काउंसिल प्रवेश (council entry) के प्रस्ताव का कड़ा विरोध करने वाले और इसके बजाय पूरी तरह से रचनात्मक कार्य तथा असहयोग पर ध्यान केंद्रित करने वाले कांग्रेस नेताओं को ऐतिहासिक रूप से क्या कहा गया था?
o: The No-Changers
The Responsivists
The Pro-Changers
The Extremists
e: Detailed Explanation: Leaders like C. Rajagopalachari, Vallabhbhai Patel, Rajendra Prasad, and M.A. Ansari opposed entering colonial assemblies. They wanted to continue the boycott and focus on grass-roots constructive work, earning the designation 'No-Changers'.

qe: At which historic annual session of the Indian National Congress in December 1922 was the Swarajist proposal of 'ending or mending' the councils formally defeated, leading to the resignation of C.R. Das?
qh: दिसंबर 1922 में भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के किस ऐतिहासिक वार्षिक सत्र में परिषदों को 'समाप्त करने या सुधारने' (ending or mending) के स्वराजवादी प्रस्ताव को औपचारिक रूप से खारिज कर दिया गया था, जिसके कारण सी.आर. दास का इस्तीफा हुआ?
o: The Gaya session
The Surat session
The Nagpur session
The Belgaum session
e: Detailed Explanation: The debate over council entry culminated in a vote at the Gaya session of the INC in December 1922. The No-Changers defeated the council entry proposal, prompting C.R. Das (President) and Motilal Nehru (Secretary) to resign from their official party posts.

qe: Following their defeat at the Gaya session, C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru formally announced the creation of which separate political organization within the broader nationalist front?
qh: गया सत्र में अपनी हार के बाद, सी.आर. दास और मोतीलाल नेहरू ने औपचारिक रूप से व्यापक राष्ट्रवादी मोर्चे के भीतर किस अलग राजनीतिक संगठन के गठन की घोषणा की थी?
o: Congress-Khilafat Swarajya Party
All India Depressed Classes Association
Social Service League
Satyashodhak Labour Front
e: Detailed Explanation: After resigning at the Gaya session, C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru established the Congress-Khilafat Swarajya Party (popularly known as the Swarajist Party) in early 1923, with C.R. Das serving as President and Motilal Nehru as a Secretary.

qe: What primary argument did the Swarajists put forward to justify entering the colonial legislative assemblies during a phase of mass passivity?
qh: जन निष्क्रियता के चरण के दौरान औपनिवेशिक विधायी विधानसभाओं में प्रवेश को सही ठहराने के लिए स्वराजवादियों ने कौन सा प्राथमिक तर्क दिया था?
o: It would open a new front to prevent undesirable elements from stuffing the councils and providing false legitimacy to government measures
It would allow them to permanently transfer the central portfolio finance to local village panchayats
It would completely dissolve the separate communal electorates introduced under the Morley-Minto reforms
It would enable them to replace the entire permanent civil bureaucracy with Indian officers within a year
e: Detailed Explanation: The Swarajists argued that entering councils was a continuation of non-cooperation by other means. It would keep up public morale during a political vacuum and block pro-government loyalists from occupying seats to legitimize arbitrary state laws.

qe: The No-Changers fiercely criticized parliamentary work, arguing that entering the assemblies would directly cause which negative development within the nationalist ranks?
qh: नो-चेंजर्स (No-Changers) ने संसदीय कार्य की तीखी आलोचना की, यह तर्क देते हुए कि विधानसभाओं में प्रवेश करने से राष्ट्रवादी रैंकों के भीतर कौन सा नकारात्मक विकास होगा?
o: Neglect of grass-roots constructive work, loss of revolutionary zeal, and political corruption
The immediate and complete financial bankruptcy of the Tilak Swaraj Fund
The total structural dissolution of all rural ashrams operating across Gujarat
Forcing the central working committee to adopt violent guerrilla parameter tactics
e: Detailed Explanation: The No-Changers maintained that entry into colonial legislatures would distract cadres from grass-roots organizing, erode their revolutionary fervor, and expose nationalist representatives to the perks, privileges, and political corruption of office.

qe: To avoid a damaging split like the one in 1907, both factions maintained coordination and reached a formal compromise at a meeting in Delhi in September 1923. What did this compromise allow?
qh: 1907 की तरह एक विनाशकारी विभाजन से बचने के लिए, दोनों गुटों ने समन्वय बनाए रखा और सितंबर 1923 में दिल्ली में एक बैठक में औपचारिक समझौता किया। इस समझौते ने क्या अनुमति दी?
o: The Swarajists were allowed to contest the upcoming elections as a distinct political group within the Congress
The absolute dissolution of the No-Changers' constructive work ashrams across Kheda and Bardoli
The mandatory appointment of Mahatma Gandhi as the permanent executive judge of the Zila Courts
A complete legislative termination of the separate communal electorates framework entirely
e: Detailed Explanation: Recognizing the need for unity under Gandhi's leadership, a compromise was struck in Delhi in September 1923. The Swarajists were officially permitted to contest the upcoming November 1923 elections as a distinct group operating within the Congress infrastructure.

qe: The official Swarajist Manifesto, released in October 1923, took a sharp anti-imperialist line. What tactical strategy did it outline if the government rejected their nationalist demands inside the councils?
qh: अक्टूबर 1923 में जारी आधिकारिक स्वराजवादी घोषणापत्र (Swarajist Manifesto) ने एक तीखा साम्राज्यवादी विरोधी रुख अपनाया। यदि सरकार ने परिषदों के भीतर उनकी राष्ट्रवादी मांगों को खारिज कर दिया, तो इसमें किस रणनीति की रूपरेखा दी गई थी?
o: A policy of uniform, continuous, and consistent obstruction within the councils to wreck them from within by creating deadlocks
The immediate physical burning of all municipal registration records across the United Provinces
Filing joint property lawsuits before a special three-judge panel of the High Court room
Directly ordering the working class to execute violent arsenal strikes across the Punjab plains
e: Detailed Explanation: The Swarajist election manifesto stated that they would present a demand for self-government inside the councils. If rejected, they vowed to execute a policy of uniform, continuous, and consistent obstruction to create legislative deadlocks and wreck the councils from within.

qe: In the general elections of November 1923, how many total elected seats did the Swarajists manage to secure within the Central Legislative Assembly, reflecting their significant electoral success?
qh: नवंबर 1923 के आम चुनावों में, स्वराजवादियों ने केंद्रीय विधानसभा के भीतर कुल कितनी चुनी हुई सीटों पर जीत हासिल की, जो उनकी महत्वपूर्ण चुनावी सफलता को दर्शाती है?
o: 42 out of 141 elected seats
72 out of 145 elected seats
15 out of 60 elected seats
45 out of 69 elected seats
e: Detailed Explanation: The Swarajist Party performed remarkably well in the November 1923 elections, capturing exactly 42 out of 141 elected seats in the central Imperial Legislative Council and a clear majority in the Central Provinces assembly.

qe: To win legislative majorities on critical political questions inside the Central Legislative Assembly, the Swarajists formed strategic coalitions with which other groups?
qh: केंद्रीय विधानसभा के भीतर महत्वपूर्ण राजनीतिक प्रश्नों पर विधायी बहुमत हासिल करने के लिए, स्वराजवादियों ने किन अन्य समूहों के साथ रणनीतिक गठबंधन बनाया?
o: The Liberals and independent members like Jinnah and Malaviya
The orthodox ulema of the Deoband School and the Faraizi commanders
The conservative pro-landlord elements of the Dharma Sabha coalition
The radical Derozian student network attached to the Hindu College
e: Detailed Explanation: Though they lacked an absolute majority on their own in the Central Assembly, the Swarajists successfully outvoted the government by forging strategic alliances and coalitions with Moderate Liberals and prominent independents like Mohammad Ali Jinnah and Madan Mohan Malaviya.

qe: Mahatma Gandhi historically presided over an annual session of the Indian National Congress only once. At which session did this occur, formally endorsing the agreement that the Swarajists would function as an integral part of the Congress?
qh: महात्मा गांधी ने ऐतिहासिक रूप से केवल एक बार भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के वार्षिक सत्र की अध्यक्षता की थी। यह किस सत्र में हुआ था, जिसमें औपचारिक रूप से इस समझौते का समर्थन किया गया था कि स्वराजवादी कांग्रेस के एक अभिन्न अंग के रूप में कार्य करेंगे?
o: The Belgaum session of December 1924
The Gaya session of December 1922
The Surat split conference of December 1907
The Nagpur structural reorganization session of December 1920
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi presided over the Congress only once—at the Belgaum session in December 1924. This session formally ratified the compromise between the two wings, integrating the Swarajists as the parliamentary front of the Congress.

qe: During the mid-1920s, the internal unity of the Swarajist Party fractured along a communal and strategic divide. What were the two competing camps that emerged within the party?
qh: 1920 के दशक के मध्य के दौरान, स्वराजवादी पार्टी की आंतरिक एकता सांप्रदायिक और रणनीतिक विभाजन के कारण टूट गई। पार्टी के भीतर उभरने वाले दो प्रतिस्पर्धी खेमे कौन से थे?
o: The Responsivists and the Non-responsivists
The Moderates and the Extremists structural wings
The Atmiya Sabha and the Dharma Sabha coalitions
The Akali satyagrahis and the Udasi mahant loyalists
e: Detailed Explanation: The Swarajist front fractured into two camps: the 'Responsivists', who favored cooperating with the government to hold offices and protect Hindu interests, and the main leadership ('Non-responsivists'), who rejected government posts and stuck to obstructionist lines.

qe: Who among the following Swarajist leaders spearheaded the 'Responsivist' faction, advocating for cooperation with the colonial government and holding office wherever possible?
qh: निम्नलिखित स्वराजवादी नेताओं में से किसने 'उत्तरदायी' (Responsivist) गुट का नेतृत्व किया, जिसने औपनिवेशिक सरकार के साथ सहयोग करने और जहाँ भी संभव हो पद संभालने की वकालत की?
o: Lala Lajpat Rai, Madan Mohan Malaviya, and N.C. Kelkar
Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, and Ajmal Khan exclusively
C. Rajagopalachari, Vallabhbhai Patel, and M.A. Ansari
Ananda Mohan Bose, Shibchandra Deb, and Umesh Chandra Datta
e: Detailed Explanation: Following the death of C.R. Das in 1925, the Responsivist faction within the Swarajists emerged under Lala Lajpat Rai, Madan Mohan Malaviya, and N.C. Kelkar, who shifted away from total obstruction to protect what they defined as Hindu interests.

qe: The Swarajist position in Bengal was severely weakened, and they lost the vital baseline support of many Muslim members. What specific policy failure caused this political alienation?
qh: बंगाल में स्वराजवादियों की स्थिति गंभीर रूप से कमजोर हो गई थी, और उन्होंने कई मुस्लिम सदस्यों का महत्वपूर्ण आधार समर्थन खो दिया। किस विशिष्ट नीतिगत विफलता के कारण यह राजनीतिक अलगाव हुआ?
o: The party failed to support the tenants' cause against the oppressive zamindars in Bengal
They actively voted to implement high export tariffs on native raw jute shipments
The leadership completely refused to establish any national schools inside the Dacca municipality
They introduced a formal resolution demanding the compulsory use of English inside village courts
e: Detailed Explanation: In Bengal, the majority of agricultural tenants were Muslim, while the zamindars were predominantly Hindu. When the Swarajist Party chose not to support pro-tenant legislation against the zamindars, they alienated the Muslim peasantry and lost the backing of Muslim legislators.

qe: In March 1926, the main leadership of the Swarajist Party withdrew from the legislatures. What program did they reiterate their faith in at this juncture?
qh: मार्च 1926 में, स्वराजवादी पार्टी के मुख्य नेतृत्व ने विधानसभाओं से अपना नाम वापस ले लिया। इस मोड़ पर उन्होंने किस कार्यक्रम में अपना विश्वास दोहराया?
o: Mass civil disobedience
Constitutional petitioning via the Dharma Sabha
The complete acceptance of the separate electorates framework
The absolute preservation of the status quo under British rule
e: Detailed Explanation: Recognizing that their obstructionist tactics had limits and the party was fragmenting, the main Swarajist leadership under Motilal Nehru walked out of the legislatures in March 1926, re-emphasizing their faith in a future campaign of mass civil disobedience.

qe: What final dynamic event in 1930 caused the remaining Swarajist members to permanently walk out of all colonial legislative assemblies?
qh: 1930 में किस अंतिम गतिशील घटना के कारण शेष स्वराजवादी सदस्यों ने सभी औपनिवेशिक विधायी विधानसभाओं से स्थायी रूप से वॉकआउट कर दिया?
o: The Lahore Congress resolution on Purna Swaraj and the beginning of the Civil Disobedience Movement
The sudden, formal enactment of the Public Safety Bill by a viceroy's ordinance
The absolute legal consolidation of the separate electorates under the Indian Councils Act
The signing of the Treaty of Sevres that completely dismembered the Ottoman caliphate
e: Detailed Explanation: The Swarajist parliamentary experiment ended permanently in 1930. Following the historic Lahore Congress resolution that declared Purna Swaraj (complete independence) as the national goal and launched the Civil Disobedience Movement, all Swarajist legislators resigned from their seats.

qe: Which prominent Swarajist leader achieved a major constitutional milestone in 1825 by being elected as the very first Indian Speaker (President) of the central Legislative Assembly?
qh: किस प्रमुख स्वराजवादी नेता ने 1925 में केंद्रीय विधानसभा के पहले भारतीय अध्यक्ष (Speaker) के रूप में चुने जाने के बाद एक प्रमुख संवैधानिक मील का पत्थर हासिल किया था?
o: Vithalbhai Patel
Motilal Nehru
C.R. Das
Rashbehari Ghosh
e: Detailed Explanation: In 1825, the Swarajists scored a major institutional victory when Vithalbhai Patel (brother of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel) was successfully elected as the first Indian Speaker (President) of the Central Legislative Assembly.

qe: In 1928, the Swarajists successfully coordinated a historic legislative defeat against which repressive government Bill that aimed to empower the state to deport foreigners?
qh: 1928 में, स्वराजवादियों ने किस दमनकारी सरकारी विधेयक (Bill) के खिलाफ एक ऐतिहासिक विधायी हार का सफलतापूर्वक समन्वय किया, जिसका उद्देश्य राज्य को विदेशियों को निर्वासित करने का अधिकार देना था?
o: Public Safety Bill
Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Bill
Seditious Meetings Restriction Bill
Indian Newspapers Registration Act
e: Detailed Explanation: Alarmed by the spread of socialist and communist ideas via international activists, the government introduced the Public Safety Bill in 1928 to deport targeted foreigners. The Swarajists and their coalition partners defeated this repressive bill in the assembly.

qe: From an analytical perspective, what primary structural drawback characterized the Swarajist strategy inside the legislative assemblies?
qh: विश्लेषणात्मक दृष्टिकोण से, विधायी विधानसभाओं के भीतर स्वराजवादी रणनीति की मुख्य संरचनात्मक कमी क्या थी?
o: They lacked a clear policy to coordinate their militancy inside legislatures with the mass struggle outside
They completely refused to participate in any budget debate or move adjournment motions
They were financially dependent on the credit lines managed by British managing agencies
They rejected any political cooperation with independent legislators like Jinnah and Malaviya
e: Detailed Explanation: A major drawback of the Swarajists was their isolation from grass-roots organizing. They failed to coordinate their parliamentary opposition inside the councils with an active mass movement outside, relying almost entirely on newspapers to communicate with the public.

qe: The No-Changers dedicated themselves entirely to grass-roots constructive work during the transition phase. In which specific geographical areas of Gujarat did their ashrams become highly successful hubs?
qh: नो-चेंजर्स ने संक्रमण चरण के दौरान खुद को पूरी तरह से जमीनी स्तर के रचनात्मक कार्यों के लिए समर्पित कर दिया। गुजरात के किन विशिष्ट भौगोलिक क्षेत्रों में उनके आश्रम अत्यधिक सफल केंद्र बने?
o: Kheda and Bardoli areas
Surat and Ahmedabad municipal zones
Barisal subdivisions
Midnapore and Guntur plains
e: Detailed Explanation: The No-Changers set up a network of rural ashrams, which became highly active in the Kheda and Bardoli districts of Gujarat. Young volunteers lived among tribals and lower-caste communities, popularizing the charkha and weaving khadi.

qe: What vital role did the grass-roots constructive workers of the No-Changers eventually serve when the national movement transitioned back into an active phase of struggle?
qh: जब राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन वापस संघर्ष के एक सक्रिय चरण में बदल गया, तो नो-चेंजर्स के जमीनी स्तर के रचनात्मक कार्यकर्ताओं ने अंततः क्या महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई?
o: They served as the organizational backbone and active organizers of civil disobedience
They were transformed into the chief executive judges of the newly consolidated High Courts
They managed the collection of land revenue shares on behalf of the district collectors
They organized a complete mass migration of the urban lower middle classes toward London
e: Detailed Explanation: Though often criticized as passive, the constructive work done by the No-Changers maintained connections with the masses during the quiet phase. These dedicated grass-roots cadres served as the organizational backbone when the next phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement was launched.

qe: A critical evaluation of the national education schools set up by the No-Changers shows that they suffered from a structural limitation during the passive phase. What was this limitation?
qh: नो-चेंजर्स द्वारा स्थापित राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा स्कूलों के एक आलोचनात्मक मूल्यांकन से पता चलता है कि वे निष्क्रिय चरण के दौरान एक संरचनात्मक सीमा से पीड़ित थे। यह सीमा क्या थी?
o: The lure of degrees and official jobs eventually drew students back to colonial schools and colleges during periods of passivity
The schools were completely banned from using local vernacular languages as the medium of instruction
They were financially dependent on the grants-in-aid provided by the Royal Commission on Decentralization
The infrastructure was restricted exclusively to the landless agricultural untouchable laborers
e: Detailed Explanation: National education institutions flourished during the excitement of the mass movement. However, during the quiet passive phase, the long-term lure of official degrees and government jobs inevitably drew students back to government-controlled schools and colleges.

qe: What was a major operational hurdle faced by the No-Changers when attempting to popularize the use of Khadi among the poor subsistence peasantry?
qh: गरीब किसानों के बीच खादी के उपयोग को लोकप्रिय बनाने का प्रयास करते समय नो-चेंजर्स द्वारा सामना की जाने वाली एक बड़ी परिचालन बाधा क्या थी?
o: Khadi was significantly costlier than the mass-imported machine-made British cloth
The colonial government passed an ordinance making the spinning of yarn a criminal capital offense
The use of the charkha was strictly restricted by upper castes to religious festivals exclusively
Khadi cloth was chemically unstable under the ambient temperature parameters of local villages
e: Detailed Explanation: While ideologically powerful, popularizing Khadi was difficult because hand-spun Khadi was significantly costlier than the cheap, mass-produced machine-made textile imports flooding the market from Manchester.

qe: Critics note that while campaigning heavily against the social stigma of untouchability, the constructive work framework of the No-Changers failed to address which critical dimension?
qh: आलोचक ध्यान देते हैं कि अस्पृश्यता के सामाजिक कलंक के खिलाफ भारी अभियान चलाने के बावजूद, नो-चेंजर्स का रचनात्मक कार्य ढांचा किस महत्वपूर्ण आयाम को संबोधित करने में विफल रहा?
o: The specific economic grievances of the landless and agricultural laborers who comprised the bulk of the untouchables
The mandatory registration of lower-caste births inside the provincial legislative councils
The direct translation of traditional Puranic scriptures into local regional vernacular mediums
Providing separate electoral colleges for the intermediate non-Brahmin communities inside Mysore
e: Detailed Explanation: A major structural critique of the No-Changers' social reform campaign was its focus on the moral and social aspects of untouchability (like temple entry or temple cleanliness) while ignoring the underlying economic grievances of the landless Dalit agricultural laborers.

qe: A survey tracking route plots a right-angled triangular configuration from depot O. A vehicle moves 24 km North, and then shifts orientation to drive 10 km East to reach target point B. Calculate the direct straight-line distance from O to B.
qh: एक कार डिपो O से 24 किमी उत्तर की ओर चलती है, और फिर दिशा बदलकर पूर्व की ओर 10 किमी जाकर बिंदु B पर पहुँचती है। O से B की सीधी रेखा की दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए।
o: 26 km
34 km
28 km
30 km
e:
Detailed Explanation: This spatial movement tracks a right-angled triangle with perpendicular legs measuring 24 km and 10 km. The direct straight-line distance is the hypotenuse.
Applying the Pythagoras theorem: $\text{Distance} = \sqrt{24^2 + 10^2} = \sqrt{576 + 100} = \sqrt{676} = \mathbf{26\text{ km}}$.

qe: In a biological ecosystem study tracking energy metrics, if the Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) of a forest tract is measured at 45,000 units and the energy accumulated as Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is 25,000 units, calculate the energy spent during plant metabolic respiration (R).
qh: ऊर्जा मापदंडों का मानचित्रण करने वाले एक पारिस्थितिकी उत्पादकता सर्वेक्षण में, यदि एक वन क्षेत्र की सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (GPP) 45,000 इकाइयाँ है और शुद्ध प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (NPP) के रूप में संचित ऊर्जा 25,000 इकाइयाँ है, तो श्वसन (R) के दौरान खर्च की गई ऊर्जा की गणना करें।
o: 20,000 units
70,000 units
30,000 units
15,000 units
e:
Detailed Explanation: Utilizing the core ecological relationship formula: $NPP = GPP - R$, we isolate respiration losses: $R = GPP - NPP$.
Substituting the given numbers: $R = 45,000 - 25,000 = \mathbf{20,000\text{ units}}$.

qe: The 'Congress-Khilafat Swarajya Party' was established with C.R. Das as its permanent President. Who among its co-founders was appointed as one of its chief Secretaries?
qh: सी.आर. दास के स्थायी अध्यक्ष के रूप में 'कांग्रेस-खिलाफत स्वराज्या पार्टी' की स्थापना की गई थी। इसके सह-संस्थापकों में से किसे इसके मुख्य सचिवों में से एक के रूप में नियुक्त किया गया था?
o: Motilal Nehru
Ajmal Khan
C. Riveragopalachari
Vithalbhai Patel
e: Detailed Explanation: Following their resignation from official Congress posts at the Gaya session, the Swarajist Party was organized with Chittaranjan Das (C.R. Das) as President and Pandit Motilal Nehru serving as one of its chief secretaries.

qe: Rethinking political avenues, what did the main leadership of the Swarajists identify as the true operational purpose of entering the colonial legislative assemblies?
qh: राजनीतिक मार्गों पर पुनर्विचार करते हुए, स्वराजवादियों के मुख्य नेतृत्व ने औपनिवेशिक विधायी विधानसभाओं में प्रवेश करने के वास्तविक परिचालन उद्देश्य के रूप में क्या पहचान की थी?
o: To use the councils as an arena of political struggle to expose their basic weaknesses and arouse popular enthusiasm from within
To cooperate fully with British managing agencies to maximize foreign capital investments
To provide legal defense counsel tracking to revolutionary terrorists facing sedition charges
To gradually transform the colonial administrative rules into a national rule through step-by-step constitutional bills
e: Detailed Explanation: The Swarajists had no intention of using the assemblies to gradually transform colonial rule. They viewed council entry as a tactical move to open a new political front, expose the weaknesses of the Montford scheme, and use the chambers as an arena of struggle to maintain public morale.

qe: Mahatma Gandhi initially opposed the Swarajist proposal of council entry upon his release from prison in February 1924. What primary factor later convinced him to reconcile and accommodate their wishes?
qh: फरवरी 1924 में जेल से रिहा होने पर महात्मा गांधी ने शुरू में स्वराजवादी परिषद प्रवेश के प्रस्ताव का विरोध किया था। बाद में किस प्राथमिक कारक ने उन्हें उनके साथ समझौता करने और उनकी इच्छाओं को स्वीकार करने के लिए आश्वस्त किया?
o: The courageous, uncompromising manner in which the Swarajists functioned in the legislatures, combined with a severe government crackdown on them and revolutionary groups in late 1924
The Swarajists voluntarily agreed to dissolve their party infrastructure and abandon council work permanently
The passing of the Public Safety Bill by a thumping majority inside the Central Legislative Assembly
A massive influx of Muslim peasant members into the regional branches of the Swarajist party in Bengal
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi changed his stance for two reasons: the Swarajists' disciplined, uncompromising performance in the legislatures proved they would not become tools of the bureaucracy, and a late 1924 government crackdown on both the Swarajists and revolutionaries prompted Gandhi to show solidarity by backing them.

qe: Following the breakdown of talks between Mahatma Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Reading in May 1921, the colonial state launched a severe crackdown. What defensive measure did the government execute to legally paralyze the nationalist volunteers?
qh: मई 1921 में महात्मा गांधी और वायसराय लॉर्ड रीडिंग के बीच बातचीत विफल होने के बाद, औपनिवेशिक राज्य ने कड़ी कार्रवाई शुरू की। स्वयंसेवकों को कानूनी रूप से पंगु बनाने के लिए सरकार ने कौन सा रक्षात्मक कदम उठाया?
o: Volunteer corps were declared illegal, public meetings were banned, and the press was gagged
The state passed a summary decree nationalizing all private property assets held by the Gujarat Vidyapeeth
The administration completely abolished the separate central and provincial list classifications
The judiciary forced all arrested political workers to undergo manual labor inside the local arsenal workshops
e: Detailed Explanation: In late 1921, as the Non-Cooperation Movement intensified, the colonial government resorted to severe repression. They outlawed all Congress and Khilafat volunteer corps, banned public assemblies, imposed strict censorship on the press, and jailed thousands of activists.

qe: The landmark Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced a highly controversial institutional mechanism that deeply damaged national unity. What was this mechanism?
qh: 1909 के ऐतिहासिक भारतीय परिषद अधिनियम (मॉर्ले-मिंटो सुधार) ने एक अत्यधिक विवादास्पद संस्थागत तंत्र पेश किया जिसने राष्ट्रीय एकता को गहरा नुकसान पहुँचाया। यह तंत्र क्या था?
o: The establishment of separate electorates for Muslims for election to the Central Council
The total legal abolition of all native vernacular media publications across codes
The absolute non-cooperation framework barring any Indian from entering the civil services
The direct physical takeover of all village community water solutions by British managing agencies
e: Detailed Explanation: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims for the first time. This institutionalized communal voting, creating deep socio-political barriers that checked the growth of national unity.

qe: Under the structural mechanics of Dyarchy introduced by the Government of India Act 1919 at the provincial level, how were the administrative subjects systematically divided?
qh: प्रांतीय स्तर पर भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1919 द्वारा शुरू किए गए द्वैध शासन (Dyarchy) के संरचनात्मक तंत्र के तहत, प्रशासनिक विषयों को व्यवस्थित रूप से कैसे विभाजित किया गया था?
o: Into 'Reserved' subjects (like law and order, finance) and 'Transferred' subjects (like education, health)
Into central maritime trading licenses and local sub-infeudation land lists
Into exclusive religious shastra portfolios and secular judicial codes
Into non-votable military expenditures and open external export duty limits
e: Detailed Explanation: Dyarchy split provincial subjects into two lists: 'Reserved' subjects (law and order, finance, land revenue, irrigation) kept under bureaucratic control; and 'Transferred' subjects (education, health, local government, agriculture) allocated to Indian popular ministers.

qe: The 'Act for Better Government of India, 1858' introduced a profound constitutional shift in the administration of the sub-continent by:
qh: ऐतिहासिक 'Act for Better Government of India, 1858' ने उपमहाद्वीप के प्रशासन में कौन सा गहरा संवैधानिक बदलाव पेश किया?
o: Transferring the power to govern from the East India Company directly to the British Crown, to be wielded through a Secretary of State
Establishing complete provincial autonomy under popular native ministerial portfolios
Abolishing the office of the Viceroy and creating the separate Federal Court structure
Scrapping the supervisory control of the British Parliament over Indian revenues
e: Detailed Explanation: Following the 1857 Revolt, the Act of 1858 dissolved the East India Company. It transferred the sovereign power to govern India directly to the British Crown, to be exercised through a cabinet post, the Secretary of State for India.

qe: The judicial framework of the Cornwallis Code of 1793 established a major milestone in modern Indian administrative history by firmly introducing which concept?
qh: 1793 के कॉर्नवॉलिस कोड के न्यायिक ढांचे ने किस अवधारणा को दृढ़ता से पेश करके आधुनिक भारतीय प्रशासनिक इतिहास में एक बुनियादी मील का पत्थर स्थापित किया?
o: The principle of the sovereignty of law and the separation of revenue and justice administration
The absolute legal immunity of all colonial government officials from civil court oversight
The mandatory use of English instead of vernacular languages across all local lower subdivisions
The total structural centralization of all judicial functions under the district Collector
e: Detailed Explanation: The Cornwallis Code of 1793 was a landmark because it established the sovereignty of law and the separation of powers. It separated revenue administration from justice, divested the Collector of judicial duties, and made government officials answerable to civil courts for official actions.

qe: The 'Treaty of Sevres', signed in May 1920 between the Allied powers and Turkey, had what direct impact on the global status of the Ottoman caliphate, deeply incensing Indian Muslims?
qh: मई 1920 में मित्र देशों की शक्तियों और तुर्की के बीच हस्ताक्षरित 'सेवर्स की संधि' (Treaty of Sevres) का ओटोमन खलीफा की वैश्विक स्थिति पर क्या सीधा प्रभाव पड़ा, जिसने भारतीय मुसलमानों को गहरा नाराज कर दिया?
o: It completely dismembered the Ottoman Empire and finalized the removal of the Khalifa from power
It successfully extended the legal control of the Khalifa over all Muslim sacred places globally
It granted absolute sovereign independence to Turkey and its neighboring Arab territories unconditionally
It forced the British Treasury to pay all administrative salaries of the Secretary of State from London funds
e: Detailed Explanation: The Treaty of Sevres completely partitioned and dismembered the Ottoman Empire, stripping the Sultan of Turkey of his territories and removing him from power. This directly targeted the religious status of the Khalifa, which incensed Muslims worldwide and drove the Khilafat agitation into its mass non-cooperation phase.
